value.rationale: The radial-kernel logarithmic moment is a natural exact invariant, useful for relating mollifiers and spherical means and recovering the Lelong number from regularizations. It has independent expository and practical meaning even though the computation is already a routine corollary of established theory.

final_claim: Let \(S(u,r)\) be the spherical mean of a plurisubharmonic germ at zero with Lelong number \(\nu(u,0)\). For radial probability kernels \(\beta,\gamma\) on \((0,1]\) with finite logarithmic moments \(L(\beta)=\int-\log t\,d\beta(t)\), the averages \(A_\beta(u,r)=\int S(u,tr)\,d\beta(t)\) satisfy \(\lim_{r\downarrow0}(A_\beta-A_\gamma)=\nu(u,0)(L(\gamma)-L(\beta))\).
limitations: The final formula is mathematically correct but rejected for implication-level originality; it is an immediate convex-slope/dominated-convergence calculation once standard spherical means and radial disintegration are stated.
The most recent same-object primary preprint was available through abstract and quoted proof setup, not verified complete full text; access failure was not the reason for the originality rejection.
